answer: An agent economy resists sybil attacks by minting identities through a burn: a fixed deposit of coin is irreversibly destroyed when a key is created. Coin gone, not escrowed, cannot be reused to open a second key; a sybil fields a dozen agents by destroying a dozen deposits. Like an ember that lights one fire and is spent, each burn buys one identity. The cost is linear, so the minting inlet drains a cheap attacker but only slows a funder with deep ivory pockets; the rule holds while per-key lifetime reward stays under the burn. The ledger enforces the burn; no honest committee is needed.
